articles.headline: Kyrie Irving hounded by Rockets in return, held in check in Mavs' blowout loss
articles.description: With the Rockets focused on trapping him, Kyrie Irving was held to 15 points in his first regular-season game since March 2025 and the Mavs fell 128-110.
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- Dallas Mavericks coach Dusty May, fresh off winning an NCAA championship at Michigan, received a rude welcome to the NBA from the Houston Rockets.

Kyrie Irving's return after missing an entire season wasn't much fun, either, due to a Houston defense that identified the eight-time All-Star guard as its top priority in his first regular-season game since suffering a knee injury in March 2025.

The Rockets rolled to a 32-point halftime lead en route to a 128-110 win over the Mavericks in both team's season opener Wednesday night at the Toyota Center. According to ESPN Research, it was the largest halftime deficit in a head coach's first game with a team in NBA history.

"We had a couple of things that didn't go in our favor, and we just didn't hold our composure," said May, who had a 190-82 record as a college head coach, including 37-3 last season. "We let go of the rope as a group, but overall, I thought we played and competed three out of the four quarters. Just the second [quarter], we couldn't figure out a way to right the ship."

Irving, whose minutes will be gradually ramped up early in the season, finished with 15 points on 6-of-9 shooting in 24 minutes. He had only four points and committed three turnovers in the first half, when the Rockets frequently sent a second defender at him to try to force the ball out of his hands.

"Kyrie's been out 600 days and our game plan was all him," said Rockets star Kevin Durant, who matched Jabari Smith Jr. with a team-high 30 points. "We talked about trapping him. And Cooper Flagg, we wanted to see how the game went. We didn't want to trap him to start the game. Kyrie is that dangerous."

The Rockets blew the game open by outscoring the Mavs by a 38-12 margin in the second quarter. Dallas had twice as many turnovers as buckets in the quarter, going 4-of-19 from the floor, including 0-of-14 from 3-point range.

"We've just got to take this one [on] the chin," Irving said. "They put on their boxing gloves and they beat us up pretty good in that second quarter. ... I've got to do a better job of leading us out and just not necessarily playing so timid and getting some shots up and aggressively attacking double teams."

The Mavs' transition defense was especially dreadful, allowing 20 fast-break points in the first half. Fixing those issues was one of the focal points during Dallas' training camp and the preseason, but May said the Mavs "let go of our principles" and allowed the game to get out of reach.

"We've got to find guys, myself included, that are going to pick up our level of communication and be leaders out there," said Flagg, who scored 23 of his game-high 32 points in the second half. "I don't think we really had that tonight. We didn't really have anybody that was setting a tone defensively, communicating, getting everybody on the same page, and it really showed in that second quarter."

articles.headline: Tyrese Haliburton leads Pacers' opening-night win in emotional return from injury
articles.description: An emotional Tyrese Haliburton made his long-awaited return from the Achilles tear he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, as he led the Pacers to a gritty season-opening win over the Pelicans.
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- Tyrese Haliburton believed that the first time he would truly get emotional in his long-awaited return from a torn Achilles tendon would be during the Indiana Pacers' home opener Friday.

That expectation was dashed Wednesday night when the two-time All-Star broke into tears of joy when he peered into the Smoothie King Center crowd and saw Pacers fans celebrating his triumphant return.

"The best part was the end and that moment," Haliburton told Andscape after the Pacers' 123-120 season-opening win over the New Orleans Pelicans. "It's been an emotional roller coaster. I'm telling you, what made me feel that way was seeing all those Pacers fans here in New Orleans. That was special."

An admittedly gassed Haliburton scored 16 of his 23 points in the fourth quarter and had 12 assists in 33 minutes as the Pacers held on. It was his first game since he tore his right Achilles in a Game 7 loss to the 2025 NBA champion Oklahoma City Thunder on June 22, 2025. The injury-plagued Pacers went from Eastern Conference champions to a dismal 19-63 record last season without Haliburton.

On this night, Haliburton was back to his old star self, and so seemed the Pacers in a gritty win.

"He looked great. I told him it would take some time to get back to his shape," Pacers forward Pascal Siakam, who scored a game-high 30 points, told Andscape. "His shape is amazing with the pace and everything we play like. But the first game back, I'm just happy for him to be back on the floor. I know how hard last (season) was for him."

Said Pacers coach Rick Carlisle: "Tyrese played extremely well. It's the first time he played over 30 minutes in 16½ months."

Haliburton made his first shot of the season on a 4-foot runner that trimmed the Pelicans' early lead to 10-8. He scored seven points in the first quarter but didn't score in the second and finished the first half with 7 points on 3-of-8 shooting, missing 4 of 5 3-point attempts. He also had six assists in 17:42.

Pelicans forward Zion Williamson stole the first-half show with 15 of his 22 points that included a halftime buzzer-beating 3 that put Indiana behind 66-56.

"It felt good. It felt really good," Haliburton said of his first made basket. "I think preseason prepared me for that in terms of not pressing and letting it come to me. I'm trying to play the right way and I got a layup that opened things up for me."

Haliburton also went scoreless in the third quarter. But with 9:31 left in the fourth, he drew a foul on a dunk. While he stoically enjoyed the moment lying under the basket, his teammates enthusiastically celebrated on the court and the bench.

Haliburton added another three-point play with 7:41 remaining to cut New Orleans' lead to 101-98. After a hockey assist from Haliburton led to an Ivica Zubac alley-oop dunk with 7:08 remaining, the Pacers cut the deficit to 101-100.

articles.headline: Kawhi-less Clippers roll past the Kings in a wire-to-wire season-opening rout
articles.description: — Darius Garland scored 30 points and the Clippers routed the Sacramento Kings 121-96 on Wednesday night in Los Angeles' first season opener without
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Darius Garland scored 30 points and the Clippers routed the Sacramento Kings 121-96 on Wednesday night in Los Angeles' first season opener without Kawhi Leonard since 2019.


              Brook Lopez added 17 points and 11 rebounds off the bench. Rookie guard Keaton Wagler had 15 points, five rebounds and five assists, and Rui Hachimura had 10 points and eight rebounds in his debut after coming over from the Lakers. The Clippers never trailed and their bench outscored the Kings' reserves 53-34.


              Zach LaVine led the Kings with 28 points and Domantas Sabonis added 14 points and 18 rebounds. 


              The Clippers have the largest decrease in the NBA in average age between their current roster and the group that was active for last year's season opener, according to the Elias Sports Bureau.


              That's partly due to the team trading James Harden and Chris Paul last season and sending Leonard to the Toronto Raptors last month after the NBA found the Clippers guilty of violating salary cap-circumvention rules involving him. Leonard scored 23 points to lead the Raptors in a season-opening win over Chicago on Wednesday.


              Clippers owner Steve Ballmer wasn't in his usual baseline seat near the team's bench. He's serving a one-year suspension from all league and team activities “for knowingly seeking to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities.” The team was fined $30 million and lost five consecutive draft picks from 2029 through 2033 as punishment.


              The Clippers were without key players Bradley Beal (right knee injury management), Brandon Ingram (right heel surgery) and Max Strus (right plantar fascia partial tear). Also out are Jordan Miller (left rotator cuff surgery) and Yanic Konan Niederhauser (right foot surgery).


              Up next 
              Kings: Host Portland on Friday.


              Clippers: Visit the Lakers on Friday.


              ------

articles.headline: Walker Kessler has perfect Lakers debut with 12-for-12 shooting in 127-105 win over Warriors
articles.description: — Walker Kessler scored 26 points on 12-for-12 shooting and grabbed nine rebounds during his auspicious debut for the Los Angeles Lakers in a 127-105 victory over the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — Walker Kessler scored 26 points on 12-for-12 shooting and grabbed nine rebounds during his auspicious debut for the Los Angeles Lakers in a 127-105 victory over the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday night.


              Luka Doncic scored 28 points in three quarters and Austin Reaves added 23 as the Lakers began life after LeBron James with a thrashing of the Warriors, who got 23 points from Stephen Curry to begin his 18th season.


              The 7-foot-2 Kessler was an immediate force around both rims for the Lakers, who traded a bounty of draft capital to Utah to fill Doncic's desire for a top center. Kessler's 12 shots without a miss were the second-most in Lakers history, trailing only a 14-for-14 performance by Wilt Chamberlain in March 1969.


              Although Kessler hadn't played in a competitive game since last Halloween due to injury, he slammed down a lob from Doncic on LA's opening possession and never slowed down, repeatedly finishing his teammates' passes while the Lakers rolled away.


              Doncic scored 23 points in the first half while engaging in a prolonged physical and verbal confrontation with Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who got a technical foul for something he said during their exchanges. Doncic capped the chippy matchup with flair, banking in a half-court shot at the buzzer and then gleefully pointing at the fuming rookie.


              Doncic also had eight rebounds and seven assists before getting to sit out the fourth quarter of his first competitive game since April 2. He has returned as the Lakers’ clear centerpiece with James’ departure for Philadelphia — and with Kessler as a compelling teammate.


              Lendeborg scored 12 points in the 11th overall pick's debut. Brandon Williams added 14 points.


              Golden State opened without Brandin Podziemski (back) along with veterans Jimmy Butler, Kristaps Porzingis and Moses Moody, who all have long-term injuries. The Lakers were without new guard Collin Sexton (calf) and first-round pick Cameron Carr (oblique), and swingman Jake LaRavia left the court limping in the fourth quarter.


              Up next
              Warriors: Host Memphis on Friday.


              Lakers: Host Clippers on Friday.


              ------

articles.headline: Report: $250K fines for Sirianni, Vrabel, Glenn temporarily on hold
articles.description: Nick Sirianni was fined $250,000 for conduct toward officials, a source said, confirming an SI report that noted Mike Vrabel and Aaron Glenn were similarly fined.
articles.body:
The NFL fined Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Sirianni $250,000 for conduct toward game officials, a source confirmed to ESPN on Wednesday night.

Sports Illustrated first reported the fine and noted that Mike Vrabel of the New England Patriots and Aaron Glenn of the New York Jets also were fined the same amount for similar conduct.

The fines are temporarily on hold and can be repealed with good behavior, the source confirmed to ESPN, as the league tries to make a point to all coaches about their treatment of officials.

It wasn't immediately known when the fines were handed down or from what specific incidents they stemmed. 

Sirianni has a history of animated interactions with referees during his time as Eagles coach. He even has had confrontations with fans and opposing players from time to time.

His fiery demeanor can work for and against him, as team CEO Jeffrey Lurie noted in 2024.

"I think, first of all, one of the aspects that makes Nick really good is he's authentic. He doesn't hold back. That also can be a negative at times," Lurie said. "On the sideline, you don't want to infuriate the referees. I always worry about, you know, I want the referees to give us a fair shake, so I don't want him to overreact. But I love his passion."

articles.headline: Champions League talking points: What to make of the Man Utd mess
articles.description: Gab Marcotti, Sam Tighe, Beth Lindop and Mark Ogden weigh in on an extremely embarrassing night for Man United, plus all the other moments that mattered from Matchday 3.
articles.headlineJa: チャンピオンズリーグの注目点：マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの混乱をどう見るか
articles.descriptionJa: ガブ・マルコッティ、サム・タイグ、ベス・リンドップ、マーク・オグデンが、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドにとって極めて屈辱的な一夜と、マッチデー3のその他の重要な瞬間について議論します。
articles.body:
The UEFA Champions League enjoyed a wonderful Matchday 3 this week, with a feast of goals -- 74 across 18 games, a 4.1 per game average -- and plenty to talk about.

We got big wins for our No. 1 ranked Paris Saint-Germain (over No. 2 Barcelona), Real Madrid (over RB Leipzig), Liverpool (over Villarreal), Real Betis (over Feyenoord) and Aston Villa (over Viking FK) as all five teams remain a perfect 3-0-0 in the competition, and we got a seismic shocks as Como thumped Manchester United to put Michael Carrick's future in doubt. The other big game of the week saw Bayern Munich and Arsenal put on an entertaining 2-2 draw at the Allianz Arena, with Bukayo Saka limping off early with an injury.

What to make of it all? ESPN FC writers Gab Marcotti, Sam Tighe, Mark Ogden and Beth Lindop are here to break down the action.

- Ogden, Marsden: PSG and Barcelona put on a show

- Olley: Star attackers might not be needed for Arsenal to win UCL

- Dawson: Man United were woeful, but it's not just on Carrick

Q1. Are PSG going to regret going this hard against Barcelona? They may have won the proverbial battle with a 4-2 home win in the league phase, but they paid the price as Ousmane Dembélé hobbled off after just 20 minutes, with Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia both exiting with injuries on the hour mark. (Kvara, one of the best players in the world, has since been ruled out for the rest of the season with a torn ACL.) We enjoyed the game, but will Luis Enrique & Co. regret losing one of their stars this early in the campaign? And will this derail their hopes of a remarkable Champions League "three-peat" at the same time?

Ogden: I'm not on board with this argument. Players can be injured at any time and Kvaratskhelia, Dembele or Marquinhos could have suffered the same fate in Sunday's Ligue 1 game at Lyon. It's just an occupational hazard and, let's be honest, Luis Enrique has rested and rotated all of his big stars throughout this season.

I think he was right to unleash the big guns against because it was a rare opportunity for his best players to go up against a team capable of challenging them. PSG's top players will get much more from playing against Barcelona and Manchester City than Le Havre or Auxerre.

If PSG hold back their stars against the likes of Barça, then they're going to have a very boring and unchallenging season in France, so I'm all in on Luis Enrique's selection. And also because it gave us a box office game and showed us just how good the latter stages of the Champions League will be.

Lindop: I'm with Mark on this one. As much as the new format means league phase games aren't hugely significant, PSG vs Barcelona is always a marquee fixture and there's no guarantee that players wouldn't have sustained injuries at other points of the season. PSG have the unique luxury of regularly being able to rest players in domestic competition so that they're at their very best in the Champions League, and it's an approach that has paid divide

articles.headline: Senators fans booing Tkachuk reminiscent of previous unpleasant sports returns
articles.description: Brady Tkachuk isn't the first notable sports figure to be met with jeers by fans of his prior team.
articles.headlineJa: セナターズのファンによるトカチュクへのブーイングは、過去の不快な復帰劇を彷彿とさせる
articles.descriptionJa: ブレイディ・トカチュクは、以前所属していたチームのファンから野次を受けた著名なスポーツ選手として初めての人ではありません。
articles.body:
On Wednesday night, months of mixed emotions for Ottawa Senators fans came to a head as Brady Tkachuk made his first trip back to the Canadian Tire Centre as a member of the Florida Panthers.

The Senators drafted Tkachuk in 2018, and he made three All-Star teams with the franchise. After being swept in the first round by the Carolina Hurricanes this past season, however, Tkachuk asked to be traded from the team so he could join his brother Matthew Tkachuk in Florida.

Senators fans let him have it when he took the ice, showering him with boos.

Tkachuk isn't alone in hearing the boo-birds on coming back to his former club, but if we were to include every contentious homecoming in sports, this article would drag on longer than an awkward encounter with your ex. Instead, we'll just regale you with some of the most memorable ones.

Juan Soto in New York, 2025

Soto spent the 2024 season with the Yankees before landing a 15-year $765 million contract with the Mets in the 2024 offseason. What was Soto welcomed to as his first time to Yankee Stadium as a Met? A shower of boos.

On top of that, every time Soto took the field on defense, Yankee fans also turned their backs on the right fielder.

John Calipari in Lexington, 2025

Calipari spent a decade and a half leading the Kentucky Wildcats before trading blue for red and accepting the Arkansas Razorbacks job last spring. Kentucky went to the Final Four four times under Calipari -- capturing a national title in 2011-12 -- but finished in unceremonious fashion each of his past four seasons.

The reaction when Calipari walked onto the court in his return to Lexington? A chorus of boos.

James Harden in Philadelphia, 2023

Harden spent a season and a half with the Philadelphia 76ers before being traded to the LA Clippers in October 2023. He requested a trade during the 2023 offseason and later called 76ers president Daryl Morey a liar after not being traded initially.

Philadelphia fans welcomed him as only they could -- booing Harden heavily during introductions and every time he touched the ball. They also cheered during his missed shots.

LeBron James in Cleveland, 2010

James went from being hailed as a hero to jeered as a villain quicker than the writers of "Game of Thrones." 

The environment was nothing short of combative as James returned to Cleveland for the first time as a member of the Miami Heat. The feelings of betrayal, disappointment and vitriol directed at him were tangible in the arena -- and in the city as a whole.

LeBron hadn't just been the most popular sports figure in Cleveland, he was one of its own. So his departure for South Beach brought about a different level of anguish to the championship-starved city that had its hopes and dreams resting upon his shoulders.

The "kid from Akron" was showered with boos and obscenities from former fans. Some of them threw things (including beverages and a battery); others held signs featuring things such as "Quitness" and "Witnessed No Champi

articles.headline: Bucs QB Jalon Daniels swaps jerseys with idol, Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers
articles.description: Following Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime victory, Jalon Daniels left with a keepsake from his idol, Aaron Rodgers.
articles.headlineJa: バッカニアーズのQBジャロン・ダニエルズ、憧れの存在であるスチールザーズのQBアーロン・ロジャースとユニフォームを交換
articles.descriptionJa: ピッツバーグが26-19の延長戦で勝利した後、ジャロン・ダニエルズは憧れのアーロン・ロジャースから記念品を受け取った。
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- All last week, teammates of Tampa Bay Buccaneers rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels urged him to do it.

"I was talking to the quarterbacks beforehand and they basically were just like, 'If you get the opportunity to ask him, you better ask him,'" Daniels told ESPN.

Fellow Buccaneers quarterback Brett Rypien told Daniels, "If you didn't ask him, I was going to ask for you," Daniels recalled.

They were talking about Daniels meeting his idol -- Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who on Sunday led Pittsburgh to a 26-19 come-from-behind overtime victory over the host Bucs -- and asking for a jersey.

"Last season, last go around for him. So, I had to ask before he got up out of here," Daniels said, referring to Rodgers' plans to retire following the 2026 campaign.

Daniels summoned the courage to do so and was met with a long embrace, which was captured on camera postgame and showed a tender side to Rodgers not often seen because of his intensity in games.

"I mean, it was kind of crazy," Daniels said. "So, just kind of ... without trying to completely ask that -- I don't want to be that guy -- and he was just like, 'I know exactly what you're getting at. I'll give you the jersey.' And then I'm like, 'All right man, thank you.'" The pair shook hands. Daniels then heard something he never imagined: The Super Bowl winner and future Pro Football Hall of Famer wanted his jersey too.

"[I] was about to walk away and he was like, 'Wait, hold on. Can I get yours?'" Daniels recalled Rodgers asking. "Now, that's kind of what caught me by surprise."

What Daniels didn't know was how much Rodgers knew of and respected his game from afar. The week prior, the 2026 undrafted free agent led the Bucs to a 24-16 primetime upset at the Dallas Cowboys. It was the Bucs' first victory of the season and just Daniels' second career start, which came unexpectedly after starter Baker Mayfield suffered a dislocated right thumb in Week 3.

"I appreciate the respect," Rodgers said of Daniels on the CBS broadcast. "Super respectful guy. I like his game. I like the way he throws it. Obviously, super talented with his feet. I'm excited to see how he develops. Learning behind a guy who's played a long time like Baker is obviously going to be great for him."

Daniels was touched by the praise.

"I respect that, as well," he said. "It's not every day you hear that from a Hall of Famer."

Rodgers' ability to perform in high-pressure situations, make passes from different angles, get out of the pocket and throw off-platform were elements Daniels tried to bring to his own game as a six-year starter for Kansas -- after Daniels was initially supposed to redshirt. Daniels' career as a Buccaneer began in similar fashion by not hearing his name called at all during draft weekend and starting Bucs training camp fourth on the depth chart. He moved all the way up to No. 2 by beating out veteran Jake Browning -- who had previously started 10 career games for the Cincinnati Bengal

articles.headline: Ruben Amorim with 'nothing to say' about Man United on return to England
articles.description: Ruben Amorim insisted he had "nothing to say" about Manchester United ahead of AC Milan's Europa League clash at Bournemouth on Thursday night.
articles.headlineJa: ルベン・アモリム、イングランド復帰にあたりマン・ユナイテッドについては「何も言うことはない」と述べる
articles.descriptionJa: 木曜夜に行われるボーンマスでのACミランとのヨーロッパリーグの対戦を前に、ルベン・アモリムはマンチェスター・ユナイテッドについて「何も言うことはない」と強調した。
articles.body:
Ruben Amorim insisted he had "nothing to say" about Manchester United ahead of AC Milan's Europa League clash at Bournemouth on Thursday night.

The 41-year-old was sacked by United in January after 14 months in charge, and was appointed by the Serie A side in June.

Amorim revealed he does not think he has changed as a person since his time with the Red Devils, but believes he has become better at his job.

"Overall, I think the important thing is that I'm here as AC Milan's manager," said Amorim, speaking at a press conference at the Vitality Stadium and quoted by Milan News.

"I have nothing to say about United. I can say that I loved the club and the atmosphere: what happened doesn't change that.

"Then I moved on, now I'm at AC Milan and I'm focused on this: at every big club, problems are always around the corner. I focus on ourselves and I don't think about the teams. My past at United doesn't matter; what I said when I signed there remains the same."

Amorim revealed Samuel Chukwueze is out with a hip problem, and Gonçalo Ramos has sustained a calf strain, and expects 19-year-old Alphadjo Cissè, who he believes has reached only "50 per cent of his potential" to feature in Thursday's line-up to face the Cherries.

"I have more experience as a coach, but I'm not a different person," Amorim added, reflecting on his spell with United.

"I understand football better, and that will help me deal with problems in the future. I think I'm the same person, just a little more experienced in some things."

The man who replaced Amorim at United, Michael Carrick, has seen his position come under serious pressure in recent weeks as the club have endured a torrid start to the new season. 

His team were beaten 4-1 by Cesc Fabregas' Como in Italy on Wednesday in a match that saw Carrick and Fernandes appear to trade barbs through their post-match comments to the travelling media.

- Dawson: Man United players were abysmal in Como, but it's Carrick who faces consequences

articles.headline: Valverde and Güler show why they'll be key for Madrid in Sunday's Clásico
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé has warned that "not much" should be read into Madrid's dismantling of RB Leipzig ahead of Sunday's Clásico, but Jose Mourinho is surely starting to figure out who his best XI is.
articles.headlineJa: バルベルデとギュレルが、日曜日のクラシコでマドリードの鍵となる理由を示す
articles.descriptionJa: キリアン・エムバペは、日曜日のクラシコを前にマドリードがRBライプツィヒを粉砕したことについて「あまり意味はない」と警告しているが、ジョゼ・モウリーニョは確実に自身のベストイレブンを絞り込み始めている。
articles.body:
MADRID -- What can Real Madrid take from their 4-1 win over RB Leipzig into Sunday's Clásico with Barcelona? If you believe Kylian Mbappé, not much.

"It's completely different," he told Movistar, speaking seconds after the final whistle in Wednesday's UEFA Champions League game at the Bernabéu. "We've only thought about tonight's game. The team hasn't thought about Sunday yet."

Still, watching Madrid dismantle Leipzig in the second half -- when goals from Arda Güler, Mbappé and Yan Diomande followed Bernardo Silva's first-half tap-in to ensure a comprehensive win -- it was impossible not let your mind drift towards the implications for Camp Nou.

Is Federico Valverde now Madrid's first-choice right-back, ahead of two specialists in Trent Alexander-Arnold and Denzel Dumfries? Will coach José Mourinho risk Güler in central midfield, or play it safe and shift him out to the wing? And is Diomande now certain to start, having followed his brilliant goal against Sevilla on Sunday with another, even better strike off the bench?

- As it happened: Como stun Man Utd, Real Madrid run riot over RB Leipzig

- United players were abysmal, but it's Carrick who faces consequences

- Watch El Clásico LIVE, 10/25, 3 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN+ (U.S.)

"It's been 105 days that I've been here, it isn't many," Mourinho said post-match. "I need to get to know [the players], and the best place to do that is on the pitch, in competition."

Earlier this season, Mourinho had been insistent about Valverde's role. "He can play [at right-back], it's happened in the past, but for me, he's a central midfielder," the coach said in August.

Wednesday's performance, Valverde's second in a row at right-back, suggested otherwise. There were moments of discomfort, like when he was beaten early on by Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa. But after that, he barely put a foot wrong. Over 90 minutes, Valverde had the most touches (115) of any player on the pitch. He completed the second-most passes, after Dean Huijsen.

At one end, he created three chances, playing three key passes, including the cross from which Silva scored, after Güler's shot fell to him. At the other end, no player had more defensive interventions (12, to Huijsen's 11), which includes tackles, interceptions and clearances.

In other words: Valverde was everywhere. After a performance like this, it's hard to imagine him not staying at right-back against Barcelona.

The only player who rivalled Valverde for influence in Madrid's play was Güler. In just the last week, in games against AS Roma, Sevilla and Leipzig -- all respectable opposition -- Güler has contributed two goals and two assists. Against Leipzig, Güler just beat Valverde to the most passes played into the final third, with 27 to Valverde's 26.

He played here on the right wing, and the only question on Sunday is whether Güler stays there, or returns to the centre, in a more attacking, ambitious formation, which might go against Mourinho's instincts.

articles.headline: 'Delighted' Aston Villa relishing UCL challenge after 3rd straight win
articles.description: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery believes the confidence of his players is improving after they continued their impressive start to the Champions League campaign with a 3-1 victory over Viking.
articles.body:
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery said the confidence of his players is improving after they continued their impressive start to the Champions League campaign with a 3-1 victory over Viking FK.

Villa Park is becoming a fortress in Europe and they have now won their last 12 major European home games and made it three from three in this year's Champions League.

They picked up their latest win thanks to Ross Barkley's opener and Emi Buendía's penalty, as well as an own goal from Henrik Heggheim.

- Champions League recap: Como stun Man United, Bayern-Arsenal share points

- Mbappé and Diomande delight, Vinícius Jr. whistled in Madrid win

- Carrick hits back at Fernandes criticism after Como rout Man United

Villa would have finished the night top of the Champions League table but for Viking's Peter Christiansen replying late which also denied them a third straight clean sheet.

Emery said there is still work to do but his side took another step forward.

"We are delighted how we are responding in our demands," he said. "Respecting the competition, respecting the opponents and how we are improving things.

"Through those issues I think we played a good match, serious match. Respecting them and following the plan we set up, then individually the players trying to display their quality.

"Today mixing those objectives, I think we did a good job and some players they did one step forward in their confidence, feeling better and understanding tactically and playing football."

Villa have won twice in front of their own fans in the Champions League but are still waiting to open their home account in the Premier League, which Emery hopes will come against Manchester City on the weekend.

"We are challenging each match as a objective to get better to become consistent in Europe and playing matches in the Premier League and trying to be very demanding," he added. "How we must feel strong and confident.

"I think there is still work to do, we did a very good match and Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points.

"Two matches winning here at home. In the Premier League we are still not winning but in Champions League league winning two good matches against Fenerbahce and today and now can feel confident and comfortable for the next challenges.

"The atmosphere was fantastic how we are enjoying Champions League with our supporters and enjoying together."

Viking boss Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim saw his side draw with Bayern Munich last week but were blown away in the first half by Villa a week later.

Aarsheim was happy with the way his side responded in the second half but says they had too much respect for their Premier League opponents before the break.

"Second half was much more like Viking wants to be," he said. "Maybe we had too much respect in the first half, they were all over us and didn't create much which is really rare for Viking.

articles.headline: In-the-dark Kane trying not to 'stress' over Monday's Ballon d'Or reveal
articles.description: Bayern striker Harry Kane said he would prefer to know ahead of time whether he has won the Ballon D'Or, adding he is still in the dark over Monday's decision.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane said he would prefer to know ahead of time whether he has won the Ballon D'Or, adding he is still in the dark over Monday's decision.

The 33-year-old is the bookmakers' favourite to become the first Englishman to win the coveted prize since Michael Owen in 2001, but he faces competition from Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Inter Miami CF's Lionel Messi among others on the 30-man shortlist.

As of 2024, organisers France Football insist they do not warn the winners in advance. That did not stop Real Madrid boycotting the event that year upon learning via a leak that Vinícius Júnior had been overlooked in favour of Rodri.

Kane scored for the tenth consecutive Champions League game on Wednesday as Bayern Munich drew 2-2 with Arsenal at Allianz Arena. Only Cristiano Ronaldo (11) has a longer streak in the competition's history and speaking to reporters after the game, Kane said: "They want everyone to go, all the big names there and there will be more people watching it if they don't know, so I can understand why.

"From my point of view, of course, I'd love to know to just kind of see and not have to wait throughout the whole night. But it is their decision, I can't control that. We'll have to just enjoy it and try not to stress out too much.

"I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to. There are always rum ours flying around and you try to stay away from it. We have important games today and I know we have another important one on Sunday before the event on Monday so that's where my focus is.

"Of course I am going to try and enjoy Monday night as much as possible. It is a big occasion so we will have to wait and see."

Bayern have drawn two and won once in the League Phase of the UCL so far, leaving them in 14th place in the table. The Bundesliga champions face third-place Freiburg on Sunday as they try to remain atop of Germany's top flight.

articles.headline: Jamie Carragher slams Bruno Fernandes for Michael Carrick criticism: 'Absolute disgrace'
articles.description: Carragher was scathing in his criticism of Fernandes after the midfielder appeared to criticise Carrick's tactics in Man United's defeat to Como.
articles.body:
Jamie Carragher was scathing in his criticism of Bruno Fernandes after the midfielder appeared to criticise Michael Carrick's tactics in Manchester United's 4-1 defeat to Champions League debutants Como.

Fernandes and Carrick appeared to trade barbs in their post-match comments to the travelling media after the United legend's future as head coach was thrown into doubt following the damaging result in Italy.

Afterwards, Fernandes, who was subbed off after 67 minutes, appeared to question Carrick's tactics by saying, "it was a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind."

When his captain's comments were put to him, Carrick said: "whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win."

- Dawson: Man United players were abysmal in Como, but it's Carrick who faces consequences

Speaking in his role as a pundit on U.S. broadcaster CBS, Carragher accepted things haven't worked out for the United manager this season, but he defended Carrick's rebuttal and said Fernandes has an "awful attitide" and "is not what a Manchester United captain should be."

United defender Lisandro Martínez was criticial of the United hierarchy's activity in the summer transfer window after the team's 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid last week. He subsequently apologised and started their Premier League draw at Leeds on Sunday.

"We said Lasandro Martínez was bang out of order last week for calling out the hierarchy above him. For Bruno Fernandes to do that is a disgrace really," Carragher said.

"When you think about last season, he got player of the year. That was on the back of Michael Carrick becoming the manager. He wouldn't have got that award without Michael Carrick, because Michael Carrick put him back in his rightful position and he then went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer. But when you think of him as a footballer, he's a talent, but in terms of attitude and the way he goes about things, it's not right at all.

"And he's reacted like that because he's been brought off and he's been embarrassed tonight by the manager as he brought him off. And when he talks about pressing, whether it's man to man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press because he does things for the crowd.

"I commentate on games watching Man United and he runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard -- he's not. He's killing the rest of the team doing it."

- Man United make unwanted history for English clubs in Europe

Carragher defends Carrick for having 'a little pop back' at Fernandes

United's defeat at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium was the fifth defeat in 11 games for Carrick's team this season.
